case_title: CENTRAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGA TION & ANR. v. MOHD. PARVEZ ABDUL KAYUUM ETC.
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302, s.120B; Arms Act s.27; Prevention of Terrorism Act s.3(1), (2), (3) and (4); s.4
confession: Confessional statements made by the accused, which have been recorded after due compliance of s. 32, as well as of s. 52 of POTA also proves involvement of each and every accused in the criminal conspiracy. The confessional statements have been duly corroborated by other evidence
aggravating_circumstances: Conspiracy leading to attempt to murder of PW-39 and fatal attack on the deceased; spreading terror among Hindu community after post-Godhra riots
high_court_outcome: High Court set aside the conviction u/s. 302/120B IPC and s. 3(1) of POT A against all the accused, while upholding conviction under rest of the provisions. High Court also reduced the sentence imposed on A-2
neutral_facts: The accused were involved in two separate incidents that were part of a common conspiracy with the motive to spread terror among the Hindu community after the post-Godhra riots. The investigation by the CBI revealed that these incidents were part of the same transaction. The accused were associated with the conspiracy leading to the attempt to murder of a witness and the fatal attack on the deceased. There is evidence of confessional statements made by the accused, which were recorded in compliance with legal procedures and corroborated by other evidence. The prosecution case was supported by forensic evidence, call records, recovery of the vehicle used for the offence, and the weapon of the offence. The accused were found to have provided logistical support, including transportation, accommodation, and mobile phones, as part of the conspiracy. The evidence included the recovery of bullets from the deceased's body, which were examined and matched to the weapon used. The trial court convicted the accused, and the High Court upheld the conviction for most of them, reducing the sentence for one accused. The Supreme Court restored the conviction and sentence for most of the accused, while dismissing the appeals for others.
